title: Artificial thymic organoid cultures: In vitro human T-cell differentiation from hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
protocol: Dissolve ascorbic acid powder in PBS to make a 30 mM (1000X) stock solution.
Prepare R-B27 medium by supplementing RPMI 1640 with 4% B-27, 30 μM ascorbic acid, 1X penicillin/streptomycin, and 1X GlutaMAX.
Reconstitute lyophilized cytokines in sterile PBS/0.1% BSA at 50 μg/ml, and store as 20-50 μl aliquots at -80°C.
Thaw cytokine aliquots and store at 4°C for up to 10 days.
Add rhIL-7 (5 ng/mL) and rhFLT3L (5 ng/mL) to R-B27 medium before each use.
Make single cell suspensions from CB, BM, MPB, or PB by diluting samples 4X with sterile PBS.
Isolate mononuclear cells (MNCs) by Ficoll-Paque gradient centrifugation as per manufacturer instructions.
Proceed to CD34+ enrichment of MNCs using the CD34 MicroBead UltraPure kit and magnetic-assisted cell sorting (MACS) following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Stain the eluted CD34+ positive fraction with anti-CD34 and anti-CD3 antibodies and DAPI.
Isolate CD34+CD3- cells by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS).
Resuspend the purified cells in R-B27 complete medium at a concentration of 1-2x10^5 cells/mL.
Keep the cells on ice until the generation of ATOs.
Activate HSPCs for 12-18 hours before transduction when lentivirus-transduced CD34+ cells are required for ATOs.
Transduce activated HSPCs for 24 hours before using in ATOs.
Harvest, wash twice to remove free viral particles from transduced cells, and resuspend in R-B27 complete medium.
Maintain MS5-hDLL1 cells in standard T75 or T150 flasks in DMEM/10% FBS.
Passage MS5-hDLL1 cells when between 70-90% confluent at a 1:10 ratio by trypsinization for 5 min. at 37°C twice a week.
Scale up MS5-hDLL1 cells for each ATO experiment by plating in T75 or T150 flasks depending on cell number required, ideally plated at least 2 days before the experiment.
Harvest MS5-hDLL1 cells using trypsin and quenching with DMEM/10% FBS when generating ATOs.
Pipette cells gently to create a single cell suspension for ATO generation.
Pass cells through a 70 μm strainer if clumps are visible during the process of creating a single cell suspension.
Resuspend cells in R-B27 complete medium and count before use in ATOs.
Prepare the required number of 6-well culture plates by adding 1 mL of ATO complete medium to each well.
Using tweezers, transfer a cell insert into each well. Only the bottom of the insert membrane should be in contact with the medium.
Set aside the prepared culture plates in the tissue culture hood until use.
Combine the required number of isolated CD34+CD3- cells and MS5-hDLL1 cells in a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 g for 5 min. using a swinging-bucket centrifuge.
Remove the supernatant carefully by aspiration using a vacuum flask and glass pipette.
Resuspend the cell pellet by briefly vortexing the tube on low to medium speed using short pulses.
Adjust the volume of the cell slurry to ~5 μL per ATO with complete R-B27.
Coat the pipette tip by pipetting medium up and down before aspirating cell slurry.
After centrifugation, remove supernatant from cell pellet and vortex.
Add 10 μL of ATO complete medium to gently resuspend the cell pellet.
Gently pipette the cell suspension to mix thoroughly.
Measure the exact volume with a pipette after mixing.
Add enough medium to obtain a final volume of 60 μL (5 μL per ATO).
Using tweezers, remove a cell insert from media and place it on the edge of the well to allow slight draining before plating.
Draw up 5 μL of cell slurry using a 10 or 20 μL pipette tip.
Gently release the cell slurry as a drop at the end of the pipette tip.
Touch the drop gently to the middle of the cell insert membrane to release it.
Gently place the cell insert back in the medium-containing well using tweezers.
Place the plate with all generated ATOs in a cell incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 after replacing the lid.
Tilt the plate to pool media on one side of the well without letting it overflow onto the surface of the cell insert.
Aspirate medium from around the cell insert using a glass pipette attached to a vacuum aspirator, leaving approximately 100-200 μL underneath the insert.
Add 1 mL of fresh, warm ATO complete medium between the cell insert and the side of the well with a P-1000 and 1 mL tip, allowing it to spread under the cell insert without direct contact.
Add 1 mL of cold MACS buffer (PBS/0.5% BSA/2mM EDTA) onto the surface of the cell culture insert using a P-1000, immersing the ATO.
Pipette up and down several times to detach the ATO from the insert membrane and mechanically disrupt the organoid, being careful not to generate excessive air bubbles.
Transfer the cell suspension to a conical tube and pass through a cell strainer to remove debris.
Wash the cell insert and well 3-4 times with cold MACS buffer and transfer all washes to the original collection tube.
Spin cells down at 300 g for 5 minutes at 4°C, and resuspend in desired medium for downstream applications.
